Subject: Clarify on-prem pricing components + SLA evidence needed

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency and the VPC options. Procurement asked me to get a clearer breakdown of the on-prem pricing components for Nexon Health: specifically we need to understand how Redwood separates the platform fee vs runtime licensing (per-node / per-seat), and how customers typically amortize the platform fee for capital accounting.

We also operate in a regulated environment: can you confirm what level of SLA you offer for on-prem (SLA for availability, mean time to respond/restore) and what evidence you can provide (SOC2, penetration test summary, audit logs)? Finally, for budget planning — do you offer onboarding or migration credits (to cover initial training and integration) and are those applied as one-time credits or amortized?

Attached is our RFI snapshot — procurement would like everything back this week if possible.

Hi Beth — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear asks. I pulled together a short explainer and high-level answers below; I'll also attach a one-page PDF that sums the options so your finance/procurement folks have something concise to circulate.

Quick answers (high level):
- Pricing components: 1) One-time deployment/setup & optional migration fee; 2) Platform fee (annual or amortized) which covers the private control plane, model catalog access, and platform-level telemetry; 3) Runtime licensing which can be structured per-dedicated-node (preferred for predictable throughput) or per-seat for small pilot footprints.
- Amortization: Customers commonly amortize the platform fee over 12, 24 or 36 months for CAPEX accounting. We can provide an invoice schedule and an amortization worksheet.
- Onboarding/migration credits: We typically offer a one-time onboarding credit tied to a committed ARR or term length (examples: 6%–12% of first-year platform fee depending on commitment). Training hours can be included as part of that credit or as a separate SOW line item.
- SLA & evidence: For Private/VPC we publish availability targets (SLAs vary by support tier). We can provide SOC2 Type II report excerpts, a penetration-test summary (redacted), and audit-log delivery options (syslog/S3 push) as part of the security package.

A few follow-ups so we can finalize numbers:
1) Expected steady-state footprint (number of dedicated nodes or approximate vCPU/GPU need)
2) Preferred billing cadence (monthly invoiced, quarterly, or upfront annual)
3) Desired support tier (Standard, Premium, Enterprise — each has different response/restoration SLOs)

If amenable I'd propose a 30-minute session with procurement + your platform engineering lead so we can run a quick estimator and agree on a proposal format for your RFP. I'll send a calendar link in a follow-up.

Attaching: redwood_onprem_pricing_explainer.pdf (short deck)

Subject: Re: Clarify on-prem pricing components + SLA evidence needed

Beth / Monica — adding a quick technical-commercial note from the solutions side.

Thanks for the context, Beth. A couple of practical options we see work well for healthcare customers:
- Node bundling: price per dedicated node with a platform fee credit baked in when customers commit to a >=24 month term. Example: 8-node bundle + platform fee amortized over 24 months gives a predictable $/token and simplifies budgeting.
- Elastic burst vs reserved capacity: if you expect spiky inference (e.g., nightly batch scoring + daytime low latency), we can model a baseline reserved node count and a burst pool; burst is charged at a lower on-demand multiplier when unused reserved capacity is available.
- Onboarding credits: we can offer a one-time onboarding credit (we typically start at 10%) to be applied against the first invoice. For larger deals (>$1.5M ARR) we frequently extend up to 15% conditional on a 24–36 month commitment.

Sample math (very rough):
- Platform fee (annual): $480k; runtime (8 nodes): $240k/year => total $720k/year. With a 24-month commit we might provide a 12% onboarding credit and discount platform fee by 15% -> first-year effective outlay reduces materially.

Operational SLAs: Standard (business-hours ticketing, 8-hour response), Premium (24x7 monitoring, 2-hour response), Enterprise (dedicated SME, 30-minute incident acknowledgement, on-call rotation). The exact MTTR targets are outlined in the SOW and depend on deployment topology and runbook integration.

I'll draft a short estimator and a sample invoice schedule (monthly & annual amortization versions) once we have expected node counts.

Cheers,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
